Not on any account seeking forgiveness by pretending that from now on we will live a better life, that we will make up for our misconduct; that can never be done.

We can never make up for past transgressions, for moment by moment we are expected to love God with all our heart, with all our strength, with all our might, and to walk in His ways to the praise of His Name.
Therefore we can never by our own doings make up for past misconduct.
But through faith in Jesus, if we put our trust in Him for salvation, the righteousness of Christ is imputed to us.

In other words, the holy work and life of the Lord Jesus is put to our account, as if we had been blameless, as if we had been without sin, as if we had walked all our days as consistently as the precious Jesus did.

His righteousness is imputed to us, and by that alone is forgiveness to be obtained—by putting our trust in Him, seeing Him hanging on the cross, shedding His blood as the Sin-bearer, who made atonement for our sins, and through whom alone we can obtain reconciliation.
“As we forgive our debtors.”
This is to be particularly noticed.
If anyone has offended us, transgressed against us, behaved improperly toward us, are we ready to forgive?
Are we habitually forgiving?

Even if it should happen many times, yet if the person who offends us and behaves improperly toward us makes confession, we are to be ready to forgive; and, supposing this is done, it is stated, “As we forgive our debtors.”
Here I would particularly mention that we are not warranted to expect answers to our prayers if we are not acting according to this.

I judge that this is very often a hindrance to obtaining answers to our prayers, because we cultivate an unforgiving spirit; we are not ready to forgive those who have offended us and behaved improperly toward us.
“Forgive us our debts, as we forgive our debtors”—that should be true of us.
“And do not lead us into temptation, but deliver us from evil.”
Our weakness, our helplessness, our nothingness remain as long as we are in the body, and we shall be liable to temptation and exposed to temptation.
The Lord Jesus Christ found this.
It may be in our case, as it was with Him, that the tempter leaves us for a season.
For a season he may not particularly seek to overpower us, but it will be only for a season; he will come again.
That, however, is only one side of the truth; and the other side of the truth is this: that God is ready to succor and help His children.
All through their pilgrimage, if they only acknowledge their weakness and come to Him and seek His assistance, He is ready to help.

Our prayer, therefore, is to be this: that God, in the riches of His grace, would allow us to be tempted no more than is absolutely needful for the glory of His Name, and for us to become more and more acquainted with His power, with His love, and with His readiness to appear on our behalf.
Then it is added, “But deliver us from evil.”
That more especially means the devil himself: “From the evil one, the wicked one, deliver us.”
For it is he who is the source of evil, and the greatest evil, since it is he who has such craftiness and is continually ready to gain an advantage over us.

Therefore, above all, our prayer should be this: “Deliver us from the wicked one, the evil one, the devil; do not allow him to gain an advantage over us”; and this prayer is to be uttered from the heart to the very last moment of our earthly pilgrimage.
We never reach such a state that we are so perfectly holy, so perfectly sinless, so perfectly Christlike, that the devil can never gain an advantage over us.
Oh, let us seek to enter into this!
I tell you, my own experience in this very thing is this: I distrust myself more than ever.

I acknowledge before God more than ever my own weakness and helplessness, and I have continually cried to God to keep me from the craftiness and the deceit of the wicked one; for were I left to myself—aged as I am, and long as I have walked in the ways of God, and in some little degree also in the fear of God, to His honor and glory, in love and holiness—yet with all this, were I left to myself, my life would end just as Asa’s did.

For thirty years he had greatly glorified God; but in the last two years of his life he deeply dishonored God. So, on account of my own weakness, my prayer continually is, “Lord, grant that I may finish my course with joy, and not to the shame and dishonor of Your holy Name.”
“For Yours is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, forever.
Amen.” These words bring before us “the why” for expecting answers to our prayers.
The kingdom is the Lord’s; He, therefore, is able to do it.
He is the Mighty One, the Powerful One.
“Yours is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, forever.”
You, O God, do not change; there is no variation found in You.
You are able to succor us.
This is further confirmed by the word “Amen.”
Yes! So it shall be.
In this evil world we shall greatly cheer and comfort ourselves by this very statement here: “Yours is the kingdom, and the power, and the glory, forever. Amen.”

Oh, how precious the prospect that we do not speak into the air, but that we speak to the loving heart of God Almighty, who can do everything and who is willing to do on behalf of His children everything that is for their real blessing in Christ!
Now, in the next and last two verses, we have what I have already referred to.
“For if you forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you; but if you do not forgive men their trespasses, neither will your Father forgive your trespasses.”

Here we see not only that we are not warranted in expecting answers to our prayers if we do not forgive our fellow men when they have offended against us and have done things that are improper, but also that we shall lose the knowledge and the enjoyment that springs from the consciousness of the forgiveness of our own sins.

It is plainly stated, “If you forgive men their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you; but if you do not forgive men their trespasses, neither will your Father forgive your trespasses.”

And I believe that in this we have the secret of why in our day so many true children of God are found whose life and conduct indicate that they are believers in Christ, but who nevertheless do not enjoy the forgiveness of their sins.

In the case of not a few, we have reason to believe it comes from there being something in their mind which they seem unable to pass over, regarding offenses they have suffered from others and have not forgiven.
If this is the case, they cannot wonder why they themselves do not enjoy the knowledge of the forgiveness of their own sins.
Now this little portion on which we have been meditating says to us afresh, “What an unspeakably blessed thing it is to be a child of God!”
So I have found it during the past seventy-one years and five months that I have been a believer in the Lord Jesus!
Oh, I cannot express to any who are not believers in the Lord Jesus Christ what they lose by staying away from Him!

There are so many who suppose that becoming a Christian is a wretched and miserable thing, that becoming a believer in Christ and giving the heart to the Lord Jesus shuts us out from life, from everything, and from every particle of enjoyment.
An altogether false notion.
The very reverse, the very reverse is the case!

I repeat what I have said more than once: that as a young man under twenty I sought happiness with all my might in the things of this world, and I had the opportunity of finding it, if it could be found in this way at all.

I was passionately fond of the theater; I was fond of the ballroom; I was found at the card table, at the billiard table, and in all kinds of worldly company, and very frequently at the head of them as a leader; but instead of finding real, true happiness, it was nothing but disappointment that I continually met with.
At last I thought, “Oh, if only I could travel a great deal, how happy that would make me!”
God allowed me to taste this.
I traveled forty-three days in succession, day after day, day after day.
I saw the most beautiful scenery to be seen under heaven; but after six weeks I became so sick of traveling that I could pass the most beautiful scenery without even looking at it.
Five weeks after that I found Jesus—I found my heavenly Friend—and the very first evening I was lying peacefully on my bed as a forgiven sinner, at peace with God.
I blessed and praised Him for it.

And without anyone having to say to me, “Now it must be out with the theater, it must be out with the card table, it must be out with the ballroom”—without anyone speaking a word to me, for I had not seen a single Christian to converse with—that was a settled matter.
I was now regenerated, born again, having obtained spiritual life after I had been dead in trespasses and sins for twenty years and five weeks.
Therefore, I say, without anyone saying a single word to me, it was a settled matter that my whole life must be changed and altered. And so it was; and what has been the result?
I instantly became a very happy young man, and I have been a happy man in my middle-aged years, and I am a happy man—yes, an exceedingly happy man—greatly advanced in years as I now am. Oh,

“If all the world my Jesus knew,
All the world would love Him too.”

s: But it is because the unconverted think it is a miserable thing to come to Christ that they stay away from Him.
The truth is this: that only, only, only through faith in the Lord Jesus can real, true happiness be obtained.

Therefore, any who have told themselves this and stayed away from Christ, let them do so no longer; let them acknowledge that they are sinners deserving nothing but punishment, and put their trust in Jesus alone for the salvation of their souls, and the result will be that they will obtain peace and joy in God, just as I found it when I was brought to Christ.
May God grant that this may speak to the hearts of those who until now have been going on thoughtlessly and carelessly, unconcerned about the things of heaven.
“Behold, what manner of love the Father has bestowed upon us, that we should be called the sons of God: therefore the world does not know us, because it did not know Him.
Beloved, now we are the sons of God, and it does not yet appear what we shall be: but we know that, when He appears, we shall be like Him; for we shall see Him as He is.
And every man who has this hope in him purifies himself, even as He is pure.”
1 John 3:1–3
Because we need again and again to be reminded of the truth contained in these verses, God directs our special attention to this little portion by placing the word “Behold” in front of it!

It is as if He meant to say, “My dear children, the whole of the revealed will of God, the whole of the Holy Scriptures, which I put into your hands, is important to be considered, to be pondered, and to be read from time to time; but there are certain portions which, because of your spiritual infirmity and because of the difficulties in which you find yourselves spiritually while passing through this vale of tears, you especially need to read from time to time, you especially need to ponder from time to time; and therefore, because of your weakness, I direct your attention to such portions.”
Now, then, let us ponder, particularly ponder, the truth contained in this little statement made in these three verses.
“Behold!” “Look at it carefully, ponder it, pray over it again and again, lay it to heart still more and more than you have been doing up to now,” our Father would say to us!
“What manner of love the Father has bestowed on us, that we should be called the sons of God.”
That is the special point to which our attention is directed in the first place.

If God had forgiven us, so that punishment had not come upon us on account of our countless transgressions, and had done no more, this would have been wondrous grace; but He has done far, far, FAR more than this.
And therefore it says, “What manner of love.”

The greatness of it is this: not only has the Lord passed over our countless transgressions and forgiven every one of them, so that we shall not be dealt with according to the thousandth part of the sins of which we have been guilty – no, not concerning even one single sin, in action, in word, or in thought – but He makes us His own children and takes us into the Heavenly Family.

We, who are by nature rebels against Him, who despise His love, who do not care in the least about Him, and who show this complete dislike and disregard of God day by day by going our own way and doing the things that are hateful to Him – we are not only forgiven, and not only shall we not be punished for one single sin out of the many tens of thousands of sins of which we have been guilty, in action, or word, or thought, or feeling, or desire, or inclination, but we are made His own children, taken into His family, and that not merely in name, but in reality.
By the power of the Holy Spirit, through belief in the gospel, He regenerates us, makes us a new creation in Christ, makes us His very own children.
He does not merely call us so, but makes us His very own children.
He gives us spiritual life, heavenly life, and so makes us His very own children.
That is the wondrous grace which we should ponder.

That is what God calls us to ponder: not to pass it by lightly, not to think little of it, but to think very, very, very much of it, and never to let it pass out of our minds until at last we get home to glory!
This is the “manner of love,” the kind of love which “the Father has bestowed upon us.”
O Lord! Help us to ponder it a thousand times more than we have pondered it so far.

O Lord! Help us, by the power of Your Holy Spirit, to lay it to heart a thousand times more than we have laid it to heart so far; and grant that, through considering it, through praying over it, through laying it to heart far more abundantly than we have done until now, our hearts may be filled with love to You and with gratitude in a way that has not yet been the case!
O grant that it may be so, for Jesus Christ’s sake, we implore You.
“Behold, what manner of love the Father has bestowed upon us.”
Now, here is a good practical point.
“Bestowed upon us”; and to be able to say, “Bestowed upon me.”
That is what I, by the grace of God, am able to say.
That is what, by the grace of God, many scores of those present here are able to say.
But is everyone able to say it?
This is what I desire, this is what I pray that God would grant to everyone present here: that each of them shall be able to say, “Has bestowed on me.”
Oh, how happy this would make us, how heavenly-minded it would make us, how dead to the world it would make us!
And in some small degree it would make us more Christlike than we have been so far!

“Bestowed upon us.” That we sinners, such as we are, rebellious sinners as we are by nature, should be called the sons of God – more literally and correctly the children of God, for it is a blessing bestowed not merely upon male believers, but upon female believers, upon all who love the Lord Jesus and trust in Him for the salvation of their souls!
Therefore, that we should be called the children of God.
Oh, how precious! Unspeakably blessed is this, that we belong to the Heavenly Family!

By nature every one of us is just as the Jews were, to whom the Lord Jesus said on one occasion, “Your father is the devil” – “for you do his works; you act according to his mind, you act according to your father the devil.”
Now, this was not only true of the Israelites, to whom the Lord was speaking; it is also true of us, while we are not believers in the Lord Jesus.

We may call ourselves children of God, and we may call God our Father, but it is not true as long as we are not trusting in the Lord Jesus Christ for the salvation of our souls; the moment, however, that we believe in the Lord Jesus Christ – however long and however much we have lived in sin, however varied our sins, however great they may have been – all is forgiven; we are regenerated through receiving the gospel, born again, and then we are truly the children of God and belong to the Heavenly Family!
Then the Holy Spirit, through the apostle, adds, “Therefore the world does not know us, because it did not know Him.”
The children are not known because the Father is not known.
As long as people are not believers in the Lord Jesus Christ, they do not know the children of God as children of God!

They may know their name, they may know their occupation, they may know where they live, how they are dressed, and similar things which belong to the outward man and to this present time; but insofar as they are the children of God, those who are themselves unconverted do not know the believers in Jesus, and the reason is given to us here: “Because they do not know the Father” of the children.
They do not know God Almighty and the Lord Jesus Christ, and therefore they do not really and truly know the children of God as children of God.
The divine life cannot be discerned by the ungodly.
“Beloved, now we are the sons of God”; “Beloved, now we are the children of God” – for the same change is to be made here.
“Now!” This little word “now” is especially to be considered, to be laid hold of, and to be greatly pondered.

It means this: while still in the body – that is, while still in weakness, beset with many infirmities in many respects, and very ignorant, in that state of weakness and helplessness in which all true believers in the Lord Jesus Christ are to a greater or lesser degree – we are nevertheless children of God; for though we are not all like John, who wrote this epistle, or like Paul, or like Peter, yet, notwithstanding all our many infirmities and weaknesses and failures and shortcomings, as surely as we put our trust in the Lord Jesus Christ for the salvation of our souls, we are already, even while still in the body, really and truly the children of God!
This is a precious truth!

And we must lay hold of this little word “now” by faith, ponder it in our hearts again and again and again, and not let it go, nor suppose that we only become children of God when we die, or when the Lord Jesus Christ comes again.
No, we are already the children of God now.

This, as you all see at once, even the youngest of believers, implies that we have a Father in heaven, and that this our Father in heaven is none other than God Almighty – the God who can do everything, to whom nothing is impossible.
See how precious this is.
Our Father can do everything!
Therefore, He is infinitely wise; He is infinitely rich; He is infinitely mighty; and His heart is full of infinite love to the weakest and feeblest of the children of God.

Therefore, suppose I have pain in my body: let me go to my Heavenly Father and speak to Him about it in all childlike simplicity, and ask Him, if it is for His glory and for my real good and profit and blessing, that He would graciously be pleased either to remove the pain entirely or else to lessen it, or, while it is necessary that it should last, that He would be pleased to sustain me under it so that I may not be overcome by it, and especially that I may not fret and complain and murmur, but take it out of His loving hand as a blessing bestowed upon me, which in the end must prove good for me.

If we are in a family trial, we should say to ourselves, “This family trial is not only very heavy for me to bear, but it will prove too much if I have to bear it myself; I will commit the matter into the hands of my Heavenly Father and ask Him to be graciously pleased to remove the trial, if it is for His honor and glory and for my real blessing.”
He is able to do it, for He can do everything, and He has proved the depth of His love by not sparing His only begotten Son, but delivering Him up for us all.

Then again, people in positions of employment, or in businesses, or carrying on a profession, find difficulties connected with their trade, connected with their business, connected with their profession.
Now, the great point is not to carry the burden ourselves, but to cast it upon the Lord.

He is willing to sustain us, willing to help us; and in doing so we pass peacefully and quietly through life; we are not inclined to fret, to complain, to murmur, and to be dissatisfied with God’s dealings with us, if we cast the burden upon Him and do not attempt to carry it ourselves!

And this is just what we should do; and this is just one of the many reasons why the Holy Spirit states here, “Now we are the children of God” – that is, while still in the body, while still surrounded by trial and difficulty, while still finding that conflict is more or less our lot.
Oh, this precious little word, “NOW.”
It contains a vast amount of deeply instructive, instructing truth.
Again, we now have the spiritual conflict; our natural evil tendencies are still in us, though we are regenerated.
The old nature is not removed; the old nature remains in us, just as it was before our faith in the Lord Jesus Christ.

It is true that we are regenerated, we are born again; it is true that we have spiritual life – but it is also true that the old nature is not dead; the old nature is still in us, and can only be kept down by prayer and meditation and pondering the Word of God, and by exercising faith continually.

And therefore, when trials come in connection with the old, evil, corrupt nature in us, we should spread the matter in all simplicity before God and say, “My Heavenly Father, I have no strength in myself; but there is almighty power with You, and Your heart is full of love to me, and You have proved Your wondrous love to me by bringing me to Jesus, and by giving Jesus for me, a poor, miserable, guilty sinner.
Now help me in this spiritual conflict of mine.
Oh, let me not be overpowered by this cunning of the devil, and on account of my spiritual weakness.
Oh, help me! Help me!
Help me!” What shall we find?
The Lord is willing to help us!
The Lord is willing to help us!!
I assure my young brothers and sisters in Christ of how He has helped me, now for seventy-one years and five months, times without number, and particularly at the beginning of the divine life in me.

Because of the evil habits I had formed as an unconverted young man, and the ungodly way in which I had been living up to the end of the twentieth year of my life, I found it extremely difficult, though truly a child of God and though hating sin and loving holiness, to overcome those evil tendencies which I had acquired.
It looked like this: “Oh, it will never be any different, and my prayer will never be answered.”
But by the grace of God I rolled my burden on Him and came to Him again and again.
So, little by little, it came about – and it was only little by little; it took some time – that these natural tendencies were overcome, and God helped me.

I mention this particularly for the comfort and encouragement of young, recently converted believers in Christ, that they should not despair, but expect help from God, for He is able and willing to help them.
Never, never, as long as we go to the Lord in our weakness and helplessness, shall we be overpowered; and just because we are the children of God now, the glory will therefore be our portion at last.

It is not that we become children of God when this life is over; no, while we are still in the body, while we are still here on earth, while we are still in great weakness and helplessness and great ignorance concerning many things, and while the devil has power over us, while he is not yet cast into the bottomless pit – even now we are the children of God, and shall have help from God just as we need it.
Oh, how comforting this word is.
Therefore let us continually ponder it, and not lose sight of it.
“Beloved, now” – in weakness; “now,” while the devil still has so much power; “now,” while in such great ignorance – “we are the children of God, and it does not yet appear what we shall be.”

Though we are now children of God, and as such have many privileges and may go continually to God for counsel, for advice, for help, for strength, for deliverance out of difficulties, for being supplied temporally and spiritually according to our need, yet with all this, great as the privileges are which we already enjoy, they are but little in comparison with what we shall have hereafter.

Therefore we must also ponder this: that while, on the one hand, this word “now” should never be lost sight of, yet on the other hand we should not forget what is written here, “It does not yet appear what we shall be.”
And what is it that will appear hereafter?
What is it that I, poor, worthless worm that I am, shall have hereafter?
What is it that I, an ignorant one, shall know hereafter?
What is it that shall be found hereafter in me, a weak one, and an erring one, and a falling one?
Oh, this is a deeply important thought.
“It does not yet appear what we shall be” – it is not yet made manifest what we shall be.
Oh, how will it be with the body?
How will it be with the soul?
How will it be with our knowledge?
How will it be with our spiritual power?
How will it be with our service for the Lord?
Oh, how will it be in every way?
An eternal blessing shall be granted to us, from then on, forever!
“It does not yet appear what we shall be, but we know that, when He appears, we shall be like Him, for we shall see Him as He is.”
When Jesus appears we shall be like Him – like Him as to His glorified body, which He has had since His resurrection.

Now, for any of us who are often in pain in the body, or who find their weakness and infirmity constantly reminding them that they are not yet at home and have not yet obtained the glorified body – oh, how precious is the thought that a day is coming when not the least particle of uneasiness will be found, nor of pain and suffering and weakness and helplessness, for we shall have a glorified body, exactly such a body as the Lord Jesus Christ has had since His own resurrection.
This is a precious, bright, glorious prospect!
And in this body, because it will be such a body as the Lord Jesus Christ has had since His resurrection, we shall know nothing of weariness.

At present we may be able to work joyfully and gladly eight, ten, or twelve hours, sometimes fourteen, or even sixteen hours a day, but at last weakness comes, because we are still in the body of humiliation and not in the glorified body.

But then, hereafter, there will be twenty-four hours’ work, and the next day the same, and the next day the same; and so the ability to work seven times twenty-four hours every week, and thirty days every month able to work the whole day.
And so it will go on, month after month, year after year, one hundred years after another, one thousand years after another, one million years after another, and so throughout eternity.
Work, work, work! Constant work to the glory of God in this our glorified body!
Oh, what bright, blessed, glorious prospects these are, if the heart enters into them.
Oh, how we are gladdened by the thought of working for God throughout eternity without the least particle of weakness, weariness, and suffering!
But this is only one part of it.
The other part is this.
We shall be perfectly holy, as the Lord Jesus Christ was during the thirty-three and a half years that He was on earth!

Never was a particle of wrong found in anything He did, never a particle contrary to the mind of God in anything He said; never was a particle found in all His thoughts, in all His desires, in all His wishes, contrary to the mind of God.
Everything was found in perfect conformity to the mind of God during the whole time that the blessed Savior was here on earth!
And so it will be with us.
We weak ones, feeble ones, shall not always be weak ones, feeble ones, but holy ones, spotless ones, pure ones, lovely ones.
Yes, lovely ones! Oh, how lovely!
Because the beauty of Christ is put upon us!
Oh, how precious these words are; and oh, if we kept them more in mind, if we entered into them, how our hearts would be full of peace and joy all day long and every day.
Now, it is on account of this that the statement is made, “It does not yet appear what we shall be; but we know that, when He appears, we shall be like Him.”
We shall be like Him!
Notice the reason why!
“We shall be like Him, for we shall see Him as He is!”
More correctly, “For we shall see Him even as He is.”
That is, we shall perfectly know the Lord Jesus Christ: in all His work and all His offices, not merely know Him as our Judge.
That is the way in which the ungodly will have to become acquainted with Him.
Every human being who is not a believer in Christ will know Him as their Judge, but we shall know Him as our Savior, as our Brother, as our Friend, as our Husband, as our Bridegroom.

We shall know Him in every one of the offices which He holds for the benefit of the Church of God; and just in proportion as we know the Lord now, we are conformed to Him; we become more and more like Him, even while we are still in the body.
The more acquainted we are with the Lord Jesus Christ, the more we are like Him; and then in the glory we shall know that Blessed One perfectly, and we shall be perfectly like Him!
What a bright and blessed prospect this is!

So our service throughout all eternity will be not only without weakness and weariness, pain and suffering, but completely according to the mind of God, completely in the same spirit in which the Lord Jesus Christ worked while in the body here on earth!
Precious, bright, glorious prospects are ours!

It is just because the world is so ignorant, so completely ignorant, of all the glorious things which are the portion of the believer in Christ, that they do not care about the things of God; for if it were known what the blessed position and portion of a child of God really is, everybody would seek to know Him, everybody would care about Him, everybody would believe in Him.
Now the last point: “And every man who has this hope in Him purifies himself, even as He is pure.”
First of all, as to the somewhat more correct literal meaning: “Every man” – that is, “everyone” – “who has this hope in Him.”
The meaning is not, “Has this hope in himself.”
That is not its meaning; rather, “has this hope regarding the Lord Jesus Christ,” that through faith in Him he will be perfectly like Christ in heaven.
“Everyone who has this hope in Him, or regarding Him, purifies himself, even as He is pure.”
That is, as truth in every way tends to increase holiness, so here we repeat the statement again.
Whoever has this hope regarding the Lord Jesus, to be made like Him in body and soul – everyone who has this hope regarding Him purifies himself.

It tends to make us increasingly holy; for just as we become acquainted with Christ and see what God has given us in Him, the more clearly, distinctly, and minutely we know this, the more fully holiness is increased in us, so that we shall be satisfied with nothing less than this: that we may continually become more and more Christlike.
We do not attain to it fully while we are in the body; yet this will be our aim more and more, more and more, more and more – to be like Christ.
We are not satisfied with having power over our natural, gross sins; we are not satisfied with this, but only with being, in spirit and in mind, more and more Christlike, gentle and loving.
Oh, how increasingly we seek to attain to this, earnestly desiring it more and more, seeking in every way to become like Christ.
And though it will never be fully attained while in the body, yet it is impossible to say to what degree we may, even while in the body, become Christlike.

Now, let this be the great lesson that we learn this evening: that because we are already children of God now, blessing, wonderful blessing, is to be obtained from our Heavenly Father; and that, because of the prospect we have before us, it is impossible to say to what degree we may become Christlike.
Now, will you who are not believers in Christ always continue in the way you have been going until now?
Shall there be no change?
If you continue on the broad way, final destruction will be your portion!
Do you long to spend a happy eternity together with the Lord in heaven?
Oh, what delight it will be to many at the last to see that not one of all who are present here is missing in heaven!

It is a personal interest I have in your spiritual welfare, and out of love for your soul, that I long to meet you in heaven; and oh, how it would increase our joy and delight in heaven at last to find not one missing, to find that this little meditation of ours on the evening of the 11th of April 1897 was not in vain.
Oh, how precious to find it so at the last!
And now, is there anyone present who says, “I will still have the world; I will still seek to enjoy the world”?
You will not be happy through this decision; be quite sure of that.
Oh, I tried your ways for twenty years and five weeks, and all I ever got was disappointment and increased guilt on my conscience.
But when I found Jesus, real happiness came.
Oh, such happiness as I cannot describe.
That was at the beginning of November 1825, and I have felt it ever since – only with this difference, that the happiness has increased more and more, more and more.

And that is what God is willing to give to you; for I suppose there is not a greater sinner present here than I was, though only twenty years of age, yet God bestowed this wondrous blessing on me; and what He did for me, and what He did for Paul, and what He did for other sinners, He is willing to do for anyone else.
Therefore, oh, let it be Christ whom you choose, and not the world any longer; for the world will never prove real, but, if continued in, will bring damnation, and only damnation.
May God grant His blessing, for Jesus Christ’s sake.
